quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No turns allowed.
No outlet.
No U-turns allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turns allowed.
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed. You often see this sign at intersections where there is heavy oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:

options.text: Allowed on the solid yellow line side.
Not allowed from either direction.
Allowed on the broken yellow line side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed on the broken yellow line side.
questions.explanation: When a broken yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, you can pass on the broken line side. You cannot pass on the solid line side.

questions.question: When entering a roundabout, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when entering a roundabout. Roundabouts are designed to be driven at low speeds.

questions.question: When driving in fog, rain, or snow, use:

options.text: Low beams.
High beams.
Fog lights only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, and snow. High beams reflect off these conditions and create glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, drive at:

options.text: The same speed as freeway traffic or close to it.
The posted speed limit.
Slower than freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as freeway traffic or close to it.
questions.explanation: Merge at or near the speed of traffic on the freeway, unless traffic is going faster than the speed limit.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while driving, you should:

options.text: Press hard on the brake and hold it.
Grip the steering wheel tightly and brake gently.
Pull over quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the steering wheel tightly and brake gently.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle straight. Slow down gradually by lifting your foot off the gas and using light braking. Move off the road to a safe place.

questions.question: When double solid yellow lines separate traffic lanes:

options.text: Passing is allowed from the left.
Passing is allowed from the right.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic is moving in opposite directions. You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop at railroads crossings, like school buses and trucks with hazardous materials.
Watch for trains from both directions.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Be careful at all railroad crossings. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. Watch for vehicles that must stop at crossings, such as school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.

questions.question: Use your horn when:

options.text: Another vehicle is blocking your way.
It may help prevent a crash.
Another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may help prevent a crash.
questions.explanation: Only use your horn to help avoid crashes. Do not use your horn to tell other drivers to go faster or get out of your way.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection at the speed limit when the light turns yellow. You should:

options.text: Slow down and go through without checking carefully.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the light will turn red soon. Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, cross carefully.

questions.question: To help the driver behind you stay at a safe distance, you should:

options.text: Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
Drive at a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at a steady speed.
questions.explanation: Drive at a steady speed and signal your turns and lane changes ahead of time. This helps the driver behind you stay at a safe distance.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes suddenly or without warning.
Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes suddenly or without warning.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes. Always signal before you change lanes to give other drivers time to react.

questions.question: Vehicles in Arizona must have liability insurance:

options.text: Only on interstates.
At all times.
Only when driven by a minor.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Every vehicle in Arizona must have liability insurance at all times. The insurance must be from an Arizona company and cover where the vehicle is mainly driven.

questions.question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, you should:

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch to high beams.
Turn your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights blind you, look toward the right edge of the road instead of ahead. This keeps your car safe until you pass the other vehicle.

questions.question: A solid red arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: You cannot turn in that direction.
You can turn in that direction after a full stop.
You can turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn in that direction.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means you cannot turn in that direction. You must stop and wait for a green signal.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Look through the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Rely only on your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: When backing up, put your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly through the rear window. Mirrors do not show what is directly behind your vehicle. Always back up slowly.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
Check the inside rearview mirror.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure it is safe.

questions.question: You want to park downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the road edge. This way, if your brakes fail, your vehicle will roll away from traffic. When parking uphill on a road with a curb, turn your wheels toward the center so your vehicle rolls into the curb if brakes fail.

questions.question: At what speed can hydroplaning begin when water is on the road?

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: Most tires can move water away at speeds up to 35 mph. Above 35 mph, tires cannot move water as well. Your tires may lose grip and slide on the water like water skis.

questions.question: What headlights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: Use your high beam headlights.
Use your parking lights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back at you and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Divided highway.
Railroad warning.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a divided highway is starting ahead.

questions.question: When is it safe to move back into the right lane after passing a vehicle on the left?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: After passing, move back into the right lane when you can see the headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: What is the danger of driving at excessive speeds?

options.text: Saves time so you can get to your destination more quickly.
Helps you maneuver around obstacles.
Increases the likelihood of serious bodily injury and death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the likelihood of serious bodily injury and death.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to poor decisions while driving.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of a road mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction of travel.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed from either side.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that bicycles may be crossing in this area.

questions.question: A traffic light just turned yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: You should proceed with caution.
You must clear the intersection before the light turns red.
You should come to a safe stop and wait for the light to turn green to proceed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should come to a safe stop and wait for the light to turn green to proceed.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming. If you have not entered the intersection, stop safely. Speeding through a yellow light is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Which is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using your high beam lights in the fog.
Staring at the road ahead of your vehicle.
Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors every two to five seconds to stay aware of hazards. Staring only ahead is unsafe. In fog, use low beam headlights, not high beams.

questions.question: Why should you not make sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses?

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot adequately see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.
Large trucks and buses, due to their size and weight, require longer distances to stop than smaller passenger vehicles.
Large trucks and buses travel at a higher speeds than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses, due to their size and weight, require longer distances to stop than smaller passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more distance to stop than smaller cars. A sudden stop in front of them is dangerous because they may not be able to stop in time.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light at an intersection mean?

options.text: The same thing as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
The same thing as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and go when it is safe. This is the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down when driving.
Make constant visual checks.
Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make constant visual checks.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and can hide in your blind spot or be missed easily. Always look carefully for motorcycles, mopeds, and scooters.
